Soham Mallick

About Me

I am a third-year PhD student in the Department of Statistics and Data Science at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. My broad research interests are in:

  • Causal Inference: Nonparametric identification and doubly robust estimation in the presence of unmeasured confounding.
  • Machine Learning: Inference-time methods for language models, including decoding algorithms and adaptive inference, with broader interests in reinforcement learning-based post-training.

Methodologically, I use tools from semiparametric theory and conformal inference.

I am fortunate to be jointly advised by Professor Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen and Professor Edgar Dobriban.

Before my PhD, I was a Research Intern at Carnegie Mellon University, where I worked on shape-constrained regression problems under Prof. Arun Kuchibhotla. I completed my Bachelors and Masters from the Indian Statistical Institute, Kolkata. My Master's Dissertation under Prof. Bodhisattva Sen at Columbia University focused on the topic of Optimal Transportation.

Beyond statistics, I enjoy playing and following chess and badminton.
